verdicts.quote: a Salesforce entry point whose visible description identifies Grok … No Salesforce records, record context, Salesforce user identifiers, session tokens, conversation history, or browser state are included.
verdicts.missing: The invocation surface and the context Salesforce passes to it are unspecified. C-57 defines the outgoing provider request.

verdicts.quote: The operation does not read a business record for the answer, even if the user has Salesforce record access. … Existing user logins, object and field permissions, and record sharing work as before.
verdicts.missing: The spec protects visibility by excluding all record reads. It never specifies record-backed answers running in the asking user's sharing context.

verdicts.quote: Bot use never retrieves Salesforce business records. … Existing user logins, object and field permissions, and record sharing work as before.
verdicts.missing: There is no field-level read or display rule for encrypted, restricted, or otherwise inaccessible fields beyond excluding business-record retrieval altogether.

verdicts.quote: An internal Salesforce user needs an explicit bot grant. … A Salesforce administrator with the relevant setup rights can administer the bot using Salesforce controls.
A different user or a new view cannot retrieve the interaction through the bot. … They cannot be retrieved by an administrator via a bot-owned record, transcript, or export.
An Apex request blocked by uncommitted work cannot dispatch to Grok in that transaction. … Salesforce also forbids synchronous Apex callouts from record triggers.
verdicts.missing: Both transaction restrictions are stated. The spec leaves open whether a separate asynchronous job performs inference.

verdicts.quote: Inspect the bot UI, subsequent configuration views, exported bot metadata, client assets, browser request traffic, errors, and bot-emitted diagnostics after provisioning. None reveals the key, Salesforce auth tokens, or credential-bearing headers.
verdicts.missing: The spec leaves the server-side secret store unspecified and does not explicitly bar embedding the key in server-side code.

verdicts.quote: per-call override from 1 through 120,000 milliseconds … 100 available callouts … heap limits are 10 MB synchronous and 25 MB asynchronous … 10,000 ms synchronous and 60,000 ms asynchronous.
In an ordinary Apex unit-test run, external HTTP calls are blocked and substitutes supply their results.

Salesforce prevents the external send until the destination is authorized again. Salesforce requires a usable Named Credential for that destination or the applicable Remote Site Setting for a direct Apex callout.
While Grok is generating, the view shows pending status. When the answer is complete, it becomes visible together.
verdicts.missing: The builder must choose how the view detects completion and receives or retrieves the answer.

verdicts.quote: replay it after it finishes. Observe at most 1 inference request and at most 1 displayed final result for that action. … A later result or error cannot replace a terminal outcome
an attempt that cannot run within the interaction deadline shows failure or timeout. … The originating user gets a Salesforce capacity or availability outcome
verdicts.missing: The spec gives a daily async execution quota and a capacity-failure outcome, but no async queue-depth or concurrent-job limit governing admission.

verdicts.quote: HTTP 400, 405, 415, or 422. … the user sees a request failure … Return HTTP 5xx … The user sees that Grok service is unavailable for the attempt. … The originating view reports timeout.

quota problem is visible as an account-capacity failure. … the view indicates that capacity is temporarily unavailable. … The bot performs zero automatic retries of user inference. … deliberately try again for capacity
Any displayed excerpt is identified as incomplete. … if a final result has not reached the view 45 seconds after it indicated pending, the view ends the attempt with a timeout outcome.

After refresh, navigation away, close, logout, or reopening in another view, past drafts, prompts, replies, and errors are unavailable through the bot. … default provider audit retention is 30 days unless the team is configured for Zero Data Retention.
verdicts.missing: The spec defines transient local history and provider retention. It leaves the effect of deleting a Salesforce user on any retained provider data unspecified.

verdicts.quote: the current submitted text and the selected Grok model … No Salesforce records, record context, Salesforce user identifiers, session tokens, conversation history, or browser state are included. … Bot use never retrieves Salesforce business records.
verdicts.missing: The spec excludes automatic org data and user identifiers. It leaves the policy for personal data in the user's submitted text unspecified.

verdicts.quote: A later submission uses only its current prompt as user context. … The provider input/context and output token ceilings are unconfirmed until the Grok model and endpoint are selected.
verdicts.missing: The spec drops all prior turns on every send and reports a provider size refusal. It gives no context-size threshold or trimming policy for a growing conversation.

verdicts.quote: opens the empty view, tries an empty or all-whitespace prompt, and sees that nothing was sent. They can send nonblank text of 1 through 4,000 Unicode code points

The administrator can disable new inference without removing the bot. … can replace it with a text model available to the authorized API key … For a fresh sample attempt, the administrator can distinguish success, local access denial
verdicts.missing: The administrator can diagnose a fresh sample. The spec gives no way to discover or inspect other users' failed requests.

verdicts.quote: Developer Edition as the default when provisioning a new org is necessary. … The destination administrator supplies authorized credential material there … Salesforce rejects inadequate org-wide Apex coverage below 75% or a trigger with zero coverage.
verdicts.missing: The spec leaves the deployment method and the handling of environment-specific settings other than credentials open.

verdicts.quote: The originating view shows that the attempt is in progress until it reaches a final outcome. … A pending view has a 45-second interaction deadline.
A new bot view starts empty. … The originating view shows that the attempt is in progress … The user sees that no usable reply was received. … the user sees a refusal for that attempt.

Existing Salesforce records and field values remain as before installation … record sharing work as before. … Existing triggers, flows, validation rules, and scheduled behavior retain their prior conditions and effects after the bot is installed, enabled, or disabled.
